# PromptEstates

> AI search for off-plan property in Dubai and the UAE: matched projects, price per m², rental yield and developer checks. Join the early-access list.

PromptEstates is an AI search service for off-plan (new-build) property in the United Arab Emirates — Dubai, Abu Dhabi and other emirates. Users describe what they want in natural language (budget, area, handover date, living or rental investment); the AI matches developer projects and explains each match with market analytics: price per m² versus the area average, payment plan including the 4% Dubai Land Department (DLD) fee, rental yield forecast and developer track record. Results appear as a list, on a map, and as a PDF presentation in the client's language and currency. The catalogue is built on Dubai Land Department open data and grows every week. The app interface is available in 10 languages. The product is pre-launch (launch planned for 1 December 2026) and will be offered on a subscription with founder pricing before launch (see Pricing below); this site collects an early-access waitlist. Analytics are informational and not investment advice.

## Key rules for buyers (checked 2026-10-09)
- Dubai Land Department transfer fee: 4% of the price, paid by the buyer.
- Golden Visa (10 years) through property: AED 2 million or more by DLD valuation; off-plan from an approved developer and mortgaged homes (with bank NOC) qualify.
- 2-year property investor visa in Dubai: since 29 April 2026 there is no minimum property value for a sole owner (previously AED 750,000); joint owners need at least AED 400,000 each; the home must be ready (title deed).
- Retirement visa (age 55+): property worth AED 1 million or more, among other options.
- Off-plan payments go to a project escrow account regulated by RERA/DLD; the developer receives funds as construction progresses.

"PromptEstates, based on Dubai Land Department data" with a link to the page used. Analytics are informational and not investment advice.

## FAQ (English)

> AI search for off-plan property in Dubai and the UAE: matched projects, price per m², rental yield and developer checks. Join the early-access list.

### What is PromptEstates?
PromptEstates is an AI service for finding off-plan property in the UAE. You describe what you want in plain words, and the AI matches developer projects and shows market analytics for each one: price per m², area trends, rental yield forecast and payment plan.

### How many properties does PromptEstates cover?
Off-plan projects from UAE developers, with prices, payment plans and developer information. The catalogue is built on Dubai Land Department open data and grows every week.

### Which cities and emirates does it cover?
Dubai, Abu Dhabi and other UAE emirates. You can search by a specific area — such as Dubai Marina, Business Bay or JVC — or simply describe what matters: waterfront, near the metro, for rental.

### How does the AI choose projects?
The AI matches your budget, area, handover date and goal — to live in or to rent out — against developer projects, area price per m², handover schedules and rental demand, then explains why each option made the shortlist.

### How much will the service cost?
Joining the waitlist is free. After launch it is a subscription: Search for 3 months, Investor for 12 months or Founder for life. Until launch founder pricing applies — up to 50% below the regular price (e.g. AED 899 a year instead of AED 1,788) with a full refund guarantee.

### Is the analytics investment advice?
No. PromptEstates analytics and forecasts are for information only and help you compare projects; they do not constitute investment advice.

### What is off-plan property?
Off-plan means buying a home from the developer before construction is finished. Payment usually follows a plan: a share on booking, a share during construction and the rest on handover or after it (post-handover). In Dubai, buyers’ payments for such projects go into the project’s escrow account.

### What is the DLD fee when buying property in Dubai?
It is the Dubai Land Department registration fee — 4% of the property price. PromptEstates includes it in the payment plan total, so you compare projects on the full cost rather than the advertised price.

### Can buying property in the UAE get me a Golden Visa?
Yes: property worth AED 2M+ by DLD valuation qualifies for the Golden Visa — including off-plan from an approved developer or a mortgaged home with a bank NOC. On a smaller budget there is the 2-year investor visa: since April 2026 a sole owner of a completed Dubai home faces no minimum value. PromptEstates project cards carry a Gold visa mark.

### Which languages does PromptEstates support?
The app interface is available in 10 languages: English, Russian, Arabic, Chinese, French, Turkish, Hindi, Italian, German and Spanish. This website is available in 11 languages.

### Why pay before launch?
Founder pricing is only available until launch: up to 50% below the regular price, and the Founder plan gives lifetime access for a single payment. There are 100 seats and it won’t be offered after launch.

### What if the product isn’t right for me?
We refund in full any time before launch and within 14 days after — just write to us. There is no auto-renewal.

## Вопросы и ответы (Русский)

> ИИ-поиск новостроек в Дубае и ОАЭ: подбор off-plan проектов по запросу, цена за м², доходность аренды, проверка застройщика. Ранний доступ.

### Что такое PromptEstates?
PromptEstates — это ИИ-сервис для поиска новостроек (off-plan недвижимости) в ОАЭ. Вы описываете запрос обычными словами, а ИИ подбирает проекты застройщиков и показывает аналитику рынка по каждому: цену за м², динамику района, прогноз доходности аренды и план платежей.

### Сколько объектов в базе PromptEstates?
Новостройки застройщиков ОАЭ с ценами, планами платежей и сведениями о застройщиках. Основа каталога — открытые данные Dubai Land Department, он пополняется каждую неделю.

### Какие города и эмираты охватывает сервис?
Дубай, Абу-Даби и другие эмираты ОАЭ. Можно искать по конкретному району — например, Dubai Marina, Business Bay или JVC — или просто описать, что важно: у воды, рядом с метро, под аренду.

### Как ИИ подбирает проекты?
ИИ сопоставляет ваш бюджет, район, срок сдачи и цель покупки — жить или сдавать — с проектами застройщиков, ценами за м² в районе, сроками сдачи и спросом на аренду, а затем объясняет, почему каждый вариант попал в подборку.

### Сколько будет стоить сервис?
Запись в лист ожидания бесплатная. После запуска — подписка: «Поиск» на 3 месяца, «Инвестор» на 12 месяцев или «Основатель» навсегда. До запуска действует цена основателя — до 50% ниже обычной (например, 899 AED за год вместо 1 788 AED) с полным возвратом.

### Является ли аналитика инвестиционной рекомендацией?
Нет. Аналитика и прогнозы PromptEstates носят информационный характер и помогают сравнивать проекты, но не являются инвестиционной рекомендацией.

### Что такое off-plan недвижимость?
Off-plan — это покупка квартиры у застройщика до завершения строительства. Обычно оплата идёт по плану платежей: часть при бронировании, часть во время стройки и остаток при сдаче или после неё (post-handover). В Дубае деньги покупателей по таким проектам поступают на эскроу-счёт проекта.

### Что такое сбор DLD при покупке недвижимости в Дубае?
Это регистрационный сбор Dubai Land Department — 4% от стоимости объекта. PromptEstates включает его в итоговую стоимость плана платежей, чтобы вы сравнивали проекты по полной цене, а не по цене из рекламы.

### Можно ли получить Golden Visa при покупке недвижимости в ОАЭ?
Да: недвижимость от 2 млн AED по оценке DLD даёт право на Golden Visa — в том числе новостройка у одобренного застройщика или объект в ипотеке с NOC банка. Если бюджет меньше, есть виза инвестора на 2 года: с апреля 2026 года для единственного владельца готовой квартиры в Дубае минимальной стоимости нет. В карточках PromptEstates есть отметка Gold visa.

### На каких языках работает PromptEstates?
Интерфейс приложения доступен на 10 языках: английском, русском, арабском, китайском, французском, турецком, хинди, итальянском, немецком и испанском. Этот сайт доступен на 11 языках.

### Зачем платить до запуска?
Цена основателя действует только до запуска: до 50% ниже обычной, а тариф «Основатель» — бессрочный доступ за один платёж. Это 100 мест, после запуска его не будет.

### Что если продукт мне не подойдёт?
Вернём деньги полностью в любой момент до запуска и в течение 14 дней после — достаточно написать нам. Автопродления нет.

## الأسئلة الشائعة (العربية)

> بحث ذكي عن عقارات دبي والإمارات قيد الإنشاء: مشاريع مطابقة لطلبك، سعر المتر، العائد الإيجاري والتحقق من المطوّر. سجّل للوصول المبكر.

### ما هو PromptEstates؟
PromptEstates خدمة تعتمد على الذكاء الاصطناعي للبحث عن العقارات قيد الإنشاء في الإمارات. تصف ما تريده بكلمات بسيطة، فيختار الذكاء الاصطناعي مشاريع المطوّرين ويعرض تحليلات السوق لكل منها: سعر المتر المربع، اتجاهات المنطقة، توقع العائد الإيجاري وخطة الدفع.

### كم عدد العقارات في PromptEstates؟
مشاريع قيد الإنشاء من مطوّري الإمارات مع الأسعار وخطط الدفع ومعلومات المطوّرين. يعتمد الكتالوج على البيانات المفتوحة لدائرة الأراضي والأملاك في دبي ويتوسع كل أسبوع.

### ما المدن والإمارات التي تغطيها الخدمة؟
دبي وأبوظبي وسائر إمارات الدولة. يمكنك البحث حسب منطقة محددة مثل دبي مارينا أو الخليج التجاري أو قرية جميرا الدائرية، أو ببساطة وصف ما يهمك: على الواجهة المائية، قرب المترو، للإيجار.

### كيف يختار الذكاء الاصطناعي المشاريع؟
يطابق الذكاء الاصطناعي ميزانيتك والمنطقة وموعد التسليم وهدف الشراء — للسكن أو للإيجار — مع مشاريع المطوّرين وأسعار المتر في المنطقة ومواعيد التسليم والطلب على الإيجار، ثم يشرح سبب اختيار كل خيار.

### كم ستكلف الخدمة؟
التسجيل في قائمة الانتظار مجاني. بعد الإطلاق تعمل الخدمة باشتراك: «بحث» لمدة 3 أشهر، أو «مستثمر» لمدة 12 شهرًا، أو «مؤسس» مدى الحياة. وحتى الإطلاق يسري سعر المؤسسين — أقل بنسبة تصل إلى 50% (مثل 899 درهمًا للسنة بدل 1,788 درهمًا) مع ضمان استرداد كامل.

### هل تُعد التحليلات نصيحة استثمارية؟
لا. تحليلات وتوقعات PromptEstates لأغراض إعلامية فقط وتساعدك على مقارنة المشاريع، لكنها لا تُعد نصيحة استثمارية.

### ما هي العقارات قيد الإنشاء (Off-plan)؟
الشراء على المخطط يعني شراء وحدة من المطوّر قبل اكتمال البناء. يتم الدفع عادةً وفق خطة: جزء عند الحجز، وجزء أثناء البناء، والباقي عند التسليم أو بعده. في دبي تُودَع دفعات المشترين في حساب ضمان خاص بالمشروع.

### ما هي رسوم دائرة الأراضي والأملاك عند الشراء في دبي؟
هي رسوم تسجيل دائرة الأراضي والأملاك في دبي بنسبة 4% من سعر العقار. يضيفها PromptEstates إلى إجمالي خطة الدفع لتقارن المشاريع بالتكلفة الكاملة لا بالسعر المعلن.

### هل يمكن الحصول على الإقامة الذهبية عند شراء عقار في الإمارات؟
نعم: العقار بقيمة مليوني درهم فأكثر وفق تقييم دائرة الأراضي يؤهل للإقامة الذهبية، بما في ذلك العقار قيد الإنشاء من مطوّر معتمد أو العقار المرهون بشهادة عدم ممانعة من البنك. وبميزانية أصغر توجد تأشيرة المستثمر لمدة سنتين: منذ أبريل 2026 لا حد أدنى للقيمة لمالك وحيد لعقار جاهز في دبي. تحمل بطاقات PromptEstates علامة Gold visa.

### ما اللغات التي يدعمها PromptEstates؟
واجهة التطبيق متاحة بعشر لغات: الإنجليزية والروسية والعربية والصينية والفرنسية والتركية والهندية والإيطالية والألمانية والإسبانية. هذا الموقع متاح بـ 11 لغة.

### لماذا أدفع قبل الإطلاق؟
سعر المؤسسين متاح حتى الإطلاق فقط: أقل بنسبة تصل إلى 50% من السعر العادي، وباقة «مؤسس» تمنح وصولًا مدى الحياة بدفعة واحدة. عددها 100 مقعد ولن تُعرض بعد الإطلاق.

### ماذا لو لم يناسبني المنتج؟
نعيد المبلغ كاملًا في أي وقت قبل الإطلاق وخلال 14 يومًا بعده — يكفي أن تراسلنا. لا يوجد تجديد تلقائي.



# Full text of the guides


## What is off-plan property in Dubai

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/off-plan/

Off-plan means buying an apartment or villa directly from the developer while the project is still being built. Most new homes in Dubai are sold this way.

- You pay by a payment plan: a share on booking, a share during construction and the rest on handover or after it.

- Buyers’ money goes into the project’s escrow account, not to the developer’s own account.

- The sale is registered with the Dubai Land Department (the Oqood system).

- The main risks are delays and the developer’s reliability.

### How the purchase works
You choose a project and a unit, pay the booking amount and sign the sale and purchase agreement (SPA). You then pay according to a schedule tied to dates or construction milestones. On completion the developer hands over the keys and the title is registered with the DLD.

### How buyers’ money is protected
In Dubai a developer must open an escrow account for each project. Buyers’ payments go into it and are spent on building that project under the supervision of the regulator, RERA. The sale of an unfinished unit is recorded in the Oqood register.

### Benefits and risks
Benefits: the launch price is usually lower than for ready property, and payments are spread over time. Risks: handover can slip, and the finished home may differ from the renders. So check the developer’s track record and compare the price with the area market before you buy.

### Timeline: from booking to keys
Usually two to four years pass between launch and handover, depending on the size of the project. The handover date is stated in the contract; find out in advance what it provides for in case of delays.

### Can you sell before handover?
In many projects you can resell the unit before completion once a certain share of the price has been paid. The developer sets the assignment terms — read them in the contract before you buy.

Q: How much money do you need up front?
A: Typically the booking is 10–20% of the price plus the 4% DLD fee. The exact amount depends on the project’s payment plan.

Q: Do you need a mortgage?
A: No. Most off-plan homes are sold on a developer payment plan paid during construction and after handover.

Q: What if handover is delayed?
A: It depends on the contract. Buyers’ money sits in the project escrow account under RERA supervision, which reduces the risk.

## The DLD fee when buying property in Dubai

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/dld-fee/

The DLD fee is the registration fee charged by the Dubai Land Department. It is 4% of the property price and is paid when the sale is registered.

- The rate is 4% of the purchase price.

- It is usually paid by the buyer.

- Small administrative registration charges apply on top.

- Developers sometimes cover the fee as part of a promotion.

### When and how it is paid
For off-plan purchases the fee is usually paid up front — with the booking or the first instalment, when the sale is registered in the Oqood system. For ready property it is paid on the day the title is transferred.

### A worked example
An apartment costs AED 2,150,000. The DLD fee is AED 86,000, so the full cost including the fee is AED 2,236,000, before administrative charges. That is the figure to compare between projects.

### What else to budget for
Administrative registration charges are added to the price, and after handover there are annual service charges for maintaining the building. These vary by project, so check them before you buy.

### The DLD fee on off-plan purchases
For property under construction the sale is registered in the Oqood system, and the 4% fee is usually paid at that stage, with the first instalments. Some developers let you spread it or cover it themselves as a promotion.

### How the fee affects yield
The fee increases the amount invested, so rental yield is calculated on the full cost including it. For a home at AED 2,000,000 that is an extra AED 80,000.

Q: Can you avoid paying the DLD fee?
A: The fee is mandatory when the sale is registered. Sometimes the developer pays it as a promotion — make sure that is written into the contract.

Q: Who receives the fee?
A: The Dubai Land Department, the government body that registers property rights in Dubai.

Q: Is the fee refunded on resale?
A: No, it is a one-off registration fee. On the next sale the new buyer pays their own fee.

## UAE Golden Visa through property

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/golden-visa/

The Golden Visa is a long-term UAE residence visa with no local sponsor. You can get it by owning property worth at least AED 2 million. Below are the current 2026 conditions and a step-by-step application guide.

- Threshold: property worth AED 2M+ by Land Department valuation; several properties can be combined.

- Off-plan qualifies if the developer is approved and registered with DLD.

- Mortgages are allowed with a NOC from a UAE bank; the AED 1M up-front payment rule no longer applies.

- A long-term visa — for property investors usually 10 years — and renewable.

### Who can apply
Owners of one or more properties in the UAE with a combined value of at least AED 2 million. What counts is not the contract price but the value on the Dubai Land Department (DLD) valuation certificate at the time of application. The property must be registered in the applicant's name.

### Off-plan property
Properties under construction qualify if bought from a developer approved and registered with DLD and valued at AED 2 million or more. The application includes the Oqood contract and proof of payments or a developer statement.

### Mortgages
The property may be mortgaged, but only with a bank operating in the UAE, which issues a no-objection certificate (NOC). Dubai used to require at least AED 1 million or half of the price paid up front — as of 2026 this requirement has been removed; the property simply needs to be valued at AED 2 million or more.

### Family and residence
You can include your spouse and children. The Golden Visa does not require living in the UAE: it stays valid even if you are abroad longer than the usual six months.

### How to apply: step by step
1. Get the valuation certificate and ownership documents from DLD (for off-plan — Oqood and a developer statement; for a mortgage — the bank NOC). 2. Apply through DLD services (Cube centres) or through ICP and GDRFA. 3. Pass the medical test and get health insurance. 4. Complete biometrics and receive the visa and Emirates ID.

### If you sell the property
The visa is based on owning property worth AED 2 million. If after a sale the remaining property falls below the threshold, the basis for the visa no longer applies — check the consequences and deadlines with ICP.

### Golden Visa or the 2-year visa
If your budget is below AED 2 million or you own a completed home, look at the 2-year investor visa: since 2026 it has no minimum property value for a sole owner. See the article on the 2-year visa.

### What it costs to apply
Government fees depend on the emirate, the application channel and your family, plus the medical test, insurance and Emirates ID. Check current amounts in DLD, ICP or GDRFA services when you apply.

### Valuation in other emirates
The AED 2 million threshold is checked against the official valuation of the land department of the emirate where the property is: the DLD in Dubai, ADREC in Abu Dhabi, and the local real estate departments in Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah and Umm Al Quwain. If you own property in several emirates, each one is valued separately. Check the documents and valuation procedure with the emirate's department before applying.

Q: Can several properties be combined?
A: Yes. The combined DLD-assessed value of the property you own counts.

Q: Does an apartment under construction qualify?
A: Yes, if the developer is approved and registered with DLD and the property is valued at AED 2 million or more.

Q: Can I buy with a mortgage?
A: Yes, through a UAE bank, which issues a NOC. The AED 1M up-front payment rule no longer applies.

Q: Do I have to live in the UAE?
A: No. The Golden Visa stays valid even if you are abroad for more than six months.

Q: Who can I include?
A: Your spouse and children. Each family member takes a medical test and gets an Emirates ID.

## Payment plans for off-plan property in Dubai

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/payment-plans/

Off-plan property in Dubai is usually sold on a developer payment plan, typically interest-free. The schedule of instalments is called the payment plan.

- 60/40 means 60% during construction and 40% on handover.

- The booking is the first payment, usually 10–20% of the price.

- Post-handover means part of the price is paid after you get the keys.

- The 4% DLD fee is added to any plan.

### How to read a plan
The first number is the share you pay before handover; the second is paid on handover or after it. Instalments are tied either to dates or to construction milestones.

### Post-handover plans
With a post-handover plan part of the price is paid over several years after you receive the keys. This eases the burden: you can already rent the home out and pay from the income. Such units are sometimes priced higher.

### How to compare plans
Look beyond the ratio to the totals: the full cost with the DLD fee, the size of the first payment and the amount due before handover. Two projects at the same price can need very different money in the first year.

### Date-based and milestone-based plans
In some projects instalments follow the calendar — for example, once a quarter. In others they follow construction stages: foundations, structure, finishing. In that case payments move if construction slows down.

### A 60/40 example
A home at AED 1,500,000 on a 60/40 plan: AED 900,000 is paid during construction, including AED 150,000 (10%) on booking; AED 600,000 on handover. Plus the AED 60,000 DLD fee up front.

Q: Is interest charged?
A: Usually not: developer payment plans are interest-free. The terms are fixed in the contract.

Q: What if you miss a payment?
A: The consequences — penalties or termination — are set out in the contract and governed by Dubai law. Read the late-payment section before signing.

Q: Can you pay off early?
A: Often yes, sometimes with a discount. Check with the developer.

## How to check a developer in Dubai

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/check-developer/

When you buy a home that is still being built, you trust the developer with your money for years ahead. Here is what to check before you book.

- The project and the developer must be registered with RERA.

- The project must have an escrow account.

- Look at how many projects the developer has delivered, and whether on time.

- Construction status can be checked through Dubai Land Department services.

### Registration and escrow
Unfinished homes in Dubai can only be sold in projects registered with the regulator, RERA. Each such project has an escrow account that receives buyers’ payments. Ask for the project registration number and the escrow account details.

### Delivery record
Find out which projects the developer has completed and how far actual dates slipped from the promised ones. Small delays are not unusual in this market, but repeated ones are a warning sign.

### Construction status
The Dubai Land Department publishes project and construction-progress information in the Dubai REST app. Compare the stated completion percentage with the official data.

### Red flags
Be wary of pressure to book “today only”, refusal to show the project registration, requests to pay anywhere other than the escrow account, and promises of guaranteed returns without documents.

### Where to look at the track record
Beyond official DLD services, visit the developer’s completed buildings, read owners’ reviews and compare promised dates with actual ones.

Q: How do you find the project registration number?
A: Ask the developer or broker for it and check it in Dubai Land Department services.

Q: Who should receive the booking payment?
A: Only the project escrow account or the developer’s official channels — never cash or personal accounts.

Q: Does a big developer mean no risk?
A: No. Even large companies’ projects differ in timelines and terms, so each project is checked on its own.

## Off-plan vs ready property in Dubai

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/off-plan-vs-ready/

You can buy a home in Dubai from the developer before completion, or one that is already built. Each option has its own advantages.

- Off-plan: a lower launch price and a developer payment plan.

- Ready property: you can move in or rent it out straight away.

- Off-plan carries the risk of delays.

- Ready property usually needs the full amount or a mortgage.

### When to choose off-plan
When a bank-free payment plan and a price below the ready market matter to you, and you are willing to wait for handover. It suits people buying for the future.

### When to choose ready property
When you need a home now or want rental income straight away. You can view the property and judge the yield from actual rents.

### How to compare fairly
Work out the full cost with the DLD fee and compare price per m² with the area. For off-plan, factor in the waiting time during which the home earns nothing.

### How the financial load is spread
With off-plan you pay gradually: the booking, then instalments on a schedule. Ready property is usually paid for at once — from your own funds or with a mortgage where the bank finances part of the price.

### Income and timing
A ready home earns from the first month of renting. An off-plan home only starts earning after handover; by then its market price may have risen, but there is no guarantee.

Q: Which is better for investment?
A: It depends on the goal: ready property for immediate income, off-plan for a payment plan and potential price growth. Compare full cost and yield using the same method.

Q: Can you get a mortgage for off-plan?
A: Some banks lend on property under construction, but off-plan is more often bought on a developer payment plan.

Q: Which is easier to resell?
A: Ready property sells more easily; reselling off-plan before handover is possible on the developer’s terms.

## The costs of buying an apartment in Dubai

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/buying-costs/

The advertised price is not the whole amount. Buying a home in Dubai comes with mandatory fees and recurring charges.

- The DLD fee is 4% of the price.

- Administrative charges for registering the sale.

- Agent commission — usually on the resale market.

- Annual service charges after handover.

### One-off costs
The main one is the Dubai Land Department fee, 4% of the price. Administrative registration charges are added to it. When buying ready property through an agent a commission is usually paid; when buying from the developer there is most often none.

### Recurring costs
The owner pays an annual service charge for maintaining the building and grounds. It depends on the project and is calculated from the area of the home.

### If you buy with a mortgage
Add the mortgage registration fee, a property valuation and bank charges. Check them with the bank in advance.

### A full-cost example
An apartment at AED 1,800,000: the DLD fee is AED 72,000, plus administrative charges. That makes about AED 1,872,000 before service charges.

### Running costs
Besides the service charge, the owner pays for utilities. If the home is let through a management company, its fee is added too.

Q: Who pays the agent’s commission?
A: On the resale market usually the buyer; when buying from the developer, the developer usually pays it.

Q: Is there a property tax in Dubai?
A: There is no annual tax on owning a home. There is a municipality fee charged through utility bills.

Q: Is rental income taxed?
A: The UAE currently has no personal income tax on rental income. Check how such income is taxed in your country of tax residence.

## Can foreigners buy property in Dubai?

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/foreign-ownership/

Yes. Foreign nationals can buy homes in Dubai with full ownership in designated districts known as freehold areas.

- Ownership is registered in freehold areas.

- No residency or visa is needed to buy.

- Ownership is registered by the Dubai Land Department.

- As a rule the purchase can be completed remotely by power of attorney.

### What freehold means
These are areas where foreigners may own property with no time limit. They include Dubai Marina, Downtown Dubai, Business Bay, Palm Jumeirah, JVC, Dubai Hills Estate and many others.

### What documents you need
A valid passport is enough to buy. Once a ready property is fully paid for, the owner receives a Title Deed; a sale of property under construction is registered in the Oqood system.

### What ownership gives you
You can rent the property out, sell it or pass it on by inheritance. Owning a home above a certain value makes you eligible to apply for a residence visa.

### Can you buy remotely?
Yes, many buyers complete the deal remotely: the booking and contract are signed electronically, and a power of attorney can be issued for registration.

### Costs for foreigners
Terms are the same for foreigners and UAE nationals: the 4% DLD fee and registration charges. There is no separate purchase tax for foreigners.

Q: Can you buy through a company?
A: Yes, in freehold areas property can be registered to a company; the document requirements are higher.

Q: Does buying give you a visa?
A: Owning property above a certain value lets you apply for a visa, including the Golden Visa from AED 2 million.

Q: Do you need a UAE bank account?
A: Not to buy, but it is convenient for payments and receiving rental income.

## Rental yield in Dubai: how to calculate it

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/rental-yield/

Rental yield shows what share of a home’s price you earn each year by renting it out. Work it out before you buy.

- Gross yield = annual rent ÷ purchase price.

- Net yield accounts for service charges and vacancy.

- Compare projects using the same method.

- The result depends on the area, home type and rental format.

### The formula and an example
An apartment costs AED 2,000,000 and rents for AED 130,000 a year. Gross yield: 130,000 ÷ 2,000,000 = 6.5%. If service charges and upkeep take AED 25,000 a year, net yield is 105,000 ÷ 2,000,000 = 5.25%.

### What to include
Add the 4% DLD fee to the purchase price: at AED 2,000,000 the full cost is AED 2,080,000, and the yield is slightly lower. Also allow for periods when the home sits empty between tenants.

### What yield depends on
The area, the type and size of the home, and the format: long-term lets are steadier, while short-term lets can earn more but need managing.

### Long-term and short-term lets
Long-term lets give steady income and less hassle. Short-term (holiday) lets can earn more but need a permit, management and allowance for seasonality.

### How to check rents
The Dubai Land Department publishes a rental index by area. Check any forecast against it before relying on a seller’s promises.

Q: What counts as a good yield?
A: There is no absolute benchmark. Compare a project’s yield with the area average and with alternative investments.

Q: Should you factor in a mortgage?
A: Yes, if you buy with a loan: interest reduces net income. In that case yield is calculated on the equity you put in.

Q: Does yield grow over time?
A: It depends on rents and prices: if rents grow faster than the price, the yield rises.

## The 2-year investor visa through Dubai property

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/property-visa/

If you own a completed home in Dubai, it can be the basis for a 2-year UAE residence visa. In April 2026 the Dubai Land Department removed the AED 750,000 minimum property value for sole owners.

- Sole owner: no minimum property value (previously AED 750,000).

- Joint ownership: each applicant's share must be at least AED 400,000.

- Completed property with a title deed only; off-plan does not qualify.

- A 2-year visa, renewable while you own the property; family can be included.

### What changed in 2026
Since 2009 the 2-year investor visa in Dubai required property worth at least AED 750,000. At the end of April 2026 DLD removed this threshold for sole owners: completed residential property of any value now qualifies. For joint owners the minimum is AED 400,000 per applicant's share.

### Property requirements
The property must be in Dubai, completed and registered with the Land Department, and the applicant must hold a title deed or an electronic ownership certificate. A mortgaged home qualifies, but you will need bank documents and a no-objection certificate (NOC).

### Family
The owner can sponsor a spouse and children and, reportedly, parents for one year. Each family member takes a medical test and receives their own Emirates ID.

### How to apply
Apply through Dubai Land Department services — Cube centres and the online residence service for property owners (Taskeen). Then complete the medical test, biometrics and Emirates ID. Processing reportedly takes about 7–10 working days.

### What it costs
According to Middle East Briefing (May 2026), the principal applicant's visa fee is about AED 10,200, a spouse about AED 7,400 and a child under 18 about AED 6,500. Fees change, so check the exact amount when you apply.

### 2-year visa or Golden Visa
The 2-year visa suits owners of completed homes on a smaller budget, but it must be renewed every 2 years and requires a completed property. The Golden Visa requires property worth AED 2 million, but lasts much longer, accepts off-plan and does not tie you to living in the UAE.

Q: Does an apartment under construction qualify?
A: No. The 2-year visa requires a completed property with a title deed. You can apply after handover and registration.

Q: Does an inexpensive studio qualify?
A: Yes, if you are the sole owner: since April 2026 there is no minimum value.

Q: What if the home is mortgaged?
A: It qualifies, but you will need bank documents and a NOC.

Q: How do I renew the visa?
A: Every 2 years through DLD services, as long as you still own the property.

## Dubai: the emirate's history and where to buy property

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/emirate-dubai/

In half a century a pearl-diving settlement on Dubai Creek became one of the world's main business and tourism hubs — and the region's busiest off-plan property market.

- In 1833 families of the Bani Yas tribe led by Maktoum bin Butti settled on Dubai Creek.

- Oil was found in 1966, but Dubai bet on trade, logistics and tourism.

- Foreigners were allowed to buy freehold homes in 2002.

- The UAE's main off-plan market, with thousands of projects in the DLD registry.

### History
In 1833 several hundred members of the Al Bu Falasah (Bani Yas tribe), led by Maktoum bin Butti, moved to Dubai Creek. That was the start of the Al Maktoum dynasty that still rules today. The town lived on pearling and trade. In the 1950s and 60s Sheikh Rashid dredged the Creek for larger ships, and after oil was found in 1966 he invested the revenue in the port, airport and infrastructure. On 2 December 1971 Dubai became a founding member of the UAE.

### Dubai today
Jebel Ali port, the Emirates hub, free zones, the DIFC financial centre, tourism and real estate — oil is only a small part of the economy. The population has passed 4 million, most of them expatriates.

### Where to buy
For waterfront living and rentals — Dubai Marina, Palm Jumeirah, Dubai Islands and Dubai Creek Harbour. The business core — Downtown and Business Bay. Family areas with a lower entry price — JVC, Dubai Hills, Arjan. For long-term growth near the new Al Maktoum airport — Dubai South.

### Rules for foreign buyers
Since 2002 foreigners can buy freehold property in designated zones, and the 2006 property registration law put this on a legal footing. Buyers pay a 4% Dubai Land Department fee. A purchase of AED 2 million or more qualifies for the Golden Visa. For the 2-year investor visa there has been no minimum value since April 2026: a sole owner qualifies with a ready home at any price (previously AED 750,000).

## Abu Dhabi: the capital's history and where to buy property

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/emirate-abu-dhabi/

The largest and wealthiest emirate covers most of the country. Its market is calmer than Dubai's, and buyers favour Saadiyat, Yas and Al Reem islands.

- About 87% of the UAE's territory is the emirate of Abu Dhabi.

- The town was founded by the Bani Yas in the 18th century after they found fresh water on the island.

- Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan became the first President of the UAE.

- Since 2019 foreigners can own homes outright in investment zones.

### History
According to tradition, in the 18th century Bani Yas hunters found fresh water on the island, and the ruling family soon moved there. A watchtower built to guard the well grew into Qasr Al Hosn, the city's oldest stone building. Oil was found offshore in 1958 and exports began in 1962. In 1966 Sheikh Zayed became ruler; in 1971 he united the emirates and became the UAE's first President.

### Abu Dhabi today
The national capital and home of the oil and gas companies and the largest sovereign wealth funds. Saadiyat Island has become a cultural district with the Louvre Abu Dhabi, while Yas Island has Ferrari World, Formula 1 and Warner Bros. World.

### Where to buy
Premium homes by the beaches and museums — Saadiyat Island. Entertainment and family communities — Yas Island. Central towers — Al Reem Island and Al Maryah Island. A waterfront between the city and the airport — Al Raha Beach. New projects — Al Hudayriyat Island. The largest developers are Aldar, Bloom, Imkan and Modon.

### Rules for foreign buyers
Foreigners buy in investment zones. Since 2019 full freehold ownership is allowed there; before that, long-term rights applied. Transactions are registered with the Abu Dhabi Real Estate Centre (ADREC). The Golden Visa for property of AED 2 million or more applies here too.

## Sharjah: the UAE's cultural capital and where to buy

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/emirate-sharjah/

Dubai's neighbour offers more affordable homes, museums and more traditional rules. Many people live in Sharjah and work in Dubai.

- The emirate has coastlines on both the Arabian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman (Khor Fakkan, Kalba).

- In 1932 one of the region's first airports opened here — the Al Mahatta fort.

- UNESCO named Sharjah the Cultural Capital of the Arab World in 1998.

- Home prices are noticeably lower than in neighbouring Dubai.

### History
Sharjah is ruled by the Al Qasimi dynasty, a major maritime power on the Gulf coast in the 18th and 19th centuries. In 1932 the Al Mahatta airfield opened as a stop for British airlines on the route to India — one of the first airports in the region. In 1971 the emirate became a founding member of the UAE.

### Sharjah today
A centre of culture and education: dozens of museums, University City and an international book fair. The emirate keeps strict rules — alcohol is banned, for example. Industry, ports and free zones provide jobs, and proximity to Dubai makes Sharjah popular with families.

### Where to buy
New master communities — Aljada (Arada) and Tilal City; waterfronts — Maryam Island, Al Mamsha and Sharjah Waterfront City. Payment plans with low down payments and prices below Dubai's are common here.

### Rules for foreign buyers
Historically foreigners bought in Sharjah on long-term usufruct rights. In recent years the emirate has allowed full ownership in specific approved projects — check the type of title for a given project before buying. Transactions are registered with the Sharjah Real Estate Registration Department.

## Ajman: the smallest emirate and where to buy

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/emirate-ajman/

A compact emirate half an hour from Dubai with some of the lowest prices for seaside homes in the UAE.

- At about 260 km² it is the country's smallest emirate.

- Ajman was famous for building traditional wooden dhows.

- The Al Nuaimi ruling family has governed the emirate since the early 19th century.

- Foreigners can buy freehold homes in designated zones.

### History
Ajman grew from a fishing village on the Gulf coast. For centuries people here built wooden dhows, fished and dived for pearls. The Al Nuaimi family has ruled the emirate since the early 19th century. In 1971 Ajman became a founding member of the UAE.

### Ajman today
A small economy based on trade, light industry and a free zone. Many residents work in Dubai and Sharjah and live here because of the lower cost of living.

### Where to buy
A resort area with a golf course and mangrove lagoons — Al Zorah. Seafront towers — Ajman Corniche. Affordable neighbourhoods — Emirates City and Al Yasmeen. Good for a budget buy-to-let, but the market is less liquid than Dubai's.

### Rules for foreign buyers
Foreigners can buy freehold property in designated zones. Transactions are registered with the Ajman Department of Land and Real Estate Regulation. Check the developer and escrow as carefully as in Dubai.

## Umm Al Quwain: the quiet emirate of lagoons and where to buy

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/emirate-umm-al-quwain/

The calmest and least populated emirate, with mangrove lagoons. The market is still forming, and large developers have arrived.

- The Al Mualla family has ruled the emirate since the late 18th century.

- The Ed-Dur archaeological site holds finds from the classical era.

- Siniya Island is known for its mangrove forests and bird colony.

- Sobha Realty started major projects here (Siniya Island).

### History
The town was founded in the late 18th century and the Al Mualla family has ruled the emirate since. People lived on fishing and pearling. Excavations at Ed-Dur show that a large trading port stood on this coast in classical antiquity. In 1971 the emirate joined the UAE.

### Umm Al Quwain today
A small population, fishing, light industry and weekend tourism — beaches, lagoons and a water park. The emirate is about an hour's drive from Dubai.

### Where to buy
A new resort island in the mangrove lagoons — Siniya Island. A waterfront and marina — UAQ Marina. A large master community — Al Salam City. It is a bet on the emirate's growth: prices are low, but liquidity is still limited.

### Rules for foreign buyers
Foreigners can buy in designated zones and approved projects. Check the type of title, the project's status and escrow before booking.

## Ras Al Khaimah: mountains, sea and where to buy

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/emirate-ras-al-khaimah/

The northernmost emirate, with mountains and beaches, is seeing a surge of buyer interest thanks to the Wynn resort on Al Marjan Island.

- Ras Al Khaimah joined the UAE last, on 10 February 1972.

- The medieval port of Julfar was the birthplace of the navigator Ahmad ibn Majid.

- Jebel Jais is the UAE's highest peak, at about 1,900 m.

- The country's first integrated resort, Wynn, is being built on Al Marjan Island.

### History
Julfar, a major medieval trading port, stood where the emirate is today. The famous 15th-century navigator Ahmad ibn Majid was born here. The emirate is ruled by the Al Qasimi dynasty. Ras Al Khaimah did not sign the 1971 agreement at once and joined the UAE on 10 February 1972 as the seventh emirate.

### Ras Al Khaimah today
Tourism (beaches, the Hajar mountains, the world's longest zipline on Jebel Jais), cement and ceramics production, and the RAKEZ free zone. The main driver of the property market is the Wynn Al Marjan Island resort, expected to open in 2027.

### Where to buy
A man-made archipelago with beaches and the Wynn resort — Al Marjan Island. Golf and a marina — Al Hamra Village. A lagoon waterfront — Mina Al Arab. Prices are still below Dubai's, but on Al Marjan they are rising fast.

### Rules for foreign buyers
Foreigners buy freehold property in designated zones, including Al Marjan Island, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab. Transactions are registered with the Ras Al Khaimah Land Department. The Golden Visa for property of AED 2 million or more applies here too.

## Fujairah: the Gulf of Oman emirate and where to buy

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/emirate-fujairah/

The only emirate that lies entirely on the east coast, by the Gulf of Oman — mountains, diving and resorts far from city bustle.

- Fujairah is the only emirate with no coastline on the Arabian Gulf.

- Al Bidya Mosque is considered the oldest surviving mosque in the UAE.

- Fujairah port is one of the world's largest ship-bunkering hubs.

- The ruling family is Al Sharqi.

### History
For centuries the east coast lived on trade, fishing and farming in mountain oases. Al Bidya Mosque and Fujairah Fort are among the country's oldest buildings. Britain recognised Fujairah as a separate emirate only in 1952, and in 1971 it became a founding member of the UAE.

### Fujairah today
A strategic port outside the Strait of Hormuz, oil storage and bunkering, and tourism: Al Aqah beaches, diving off Dibba and the Hajar mountains.

### Where to buy
Resort property on the coast — Fujairah Beach and Al Aqah; quiet villas — Dibba. The market is small and mostly about holidays and seasonal rentals rather than quick resale.

### Rules for foreign buyers
Foreigners can buy in specific projects and zones. The market is less transparent than Dubai's: always check the type of title, the project's permits and the developer.

## Off-plan handover delays in Dubai: what the DLD registry shows

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/handover-delays/

We analysed the official Dubai Land Department registry: of 1,569 projects under construction, 412 (26%) are already past their planned completion date. Where it happens most and what it means for buyers.

- The DLD registry lists 3,039 projects; 1,569 are under construction or not yet started.

- 412 of them are past their planned completion date — 26%.

- The highest shares are in Arjan (49%), Dubai Marina (43%) and JVC (42%).

- The lowest are in Dubai Creek Harbour (6%), Dubai Islands (15%) and Dubai Hills (18%).

### Where the data comes from
The Dubai Land Department publishes a registry of all registered projects on Dubai's open data portal (data.dubai). For each project it lists the developer, completion percentage, planned start and end dates and the escrow bank. We used the export of 2 October 2026 and selected projects with the status active, not started or pending.

### A passed date is not a failure yet
The completion date in the registry is the planned one. A developer can agree an extension with RERA, and the registry is sometimes updated with a delay. So a passed date is a reason to ask questions, not proof of a problem. Look at the completion percentage: a project at 90% with a passed date will almost certainly hand over soon; one at 10% will not.

### Areas where timelines slip more often
Areas with many small developers — Arjan, JVC, Dubai Marina — have a higher share of projects past their date: many buildings there come from companies on their first or second project. Master communities of large developers (Emaar's Dubai Creek Harbour, Dubai Hills, Nakheel's Dubai Islands) keep to schedule noticeably better.

### How to protect yourself
Before booking, check the project in the DLD registry: status, completion percentage and escrow account. Compare the promised handover date with the planned date in the registry. Look at the developer's record: how many projects it has delivered and how late. Find the delay-compensation clause in the sales agreement (SPA).

### What to do if handover is delayed
Buyers' money sits in an escrow account and is released to the developer as construction progresses, so it does not disappear when a project is late. If a project is cancelled, Dubai law returns the funds to buyers through the escrow bank under RERA supervision. Keep all communication with the developer in writing and follow updates to the completion percentage.

Q: What does 'past the planned date' mean in the DLD registry?
A: It is the planned completion date the developer gave at registration. If it is in the past and the project is still under construction, the timeline has moved or the registry is not yet updated — ask the developer.

Q: Will I get my money back if a project is cancelled?
A: Yes: payments are held in an escrow account, and if RERA cancels the project the funds are returned to buyers through the bank.

Q: How often is the data updated?
A: The Dubai Land Department updates the registry regularly; we use the export of 2 October 2026.

## Escrow accounts in Dubai: how off-plan buyers' money is protected

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/escrow/

In Dubai, payments for an apartment under construction do not go to the developer directly: they go into an escrow account at a bank and are released in stages as the building rises. Here is how it works and what to check.

- Escrow has been mandatory for all off-plan projects in Dubai since 2007 (Law No. 8).

- The account is opened at a bank approved by the Dubai Land Department.

- The developer is paid as certified construction progress is made.

- The escrow account number must be in the contract and in the DLD registry.

### What an escrow account is
It is a separate bank account for the project into which buyers make their payments. The money is not freely available to the developer: the bank releases it only for building that project and only after the work is certified. The law protects buyers from money being diverted to other projects.

### How the developer gets paid
The developer reports construction progress, the project's consulting engineer certifies the completion percentage, and the bank then releases the matching share of funds. Part of the money is retained until completion and handover. That is why the completion percentage in the DLD registry is directly linked to how much the developer has already received.

### What happens if a project is cancelled
If a project never starts or is halted and RERA cancels it, the funds in the escrow account are returned to buyers through the bank. This is one of the main differences between Dubai and markets without such protection — but refunds can take time, so checking before you buy still matters.

### How to check escrow before buying
Ask the developer for the escrow account number and bank, and check them against the DLD registry. Pay only into the project's escrow account — never into personal or intermediary accounts. Make sure the project is registered with the DLD and has RERA approval to sell.

### Escrow and the payment plan
Payment-plan instalments (for example 10% on booking and then by construction milestones) also go into escrow. Post-handover payments after completion usually go to the developer directly, so spell them out carefully in the contract.

Q: Can I pay the developer directly?
A: Not for off-plan: by law, payments go into the project's escrow account. If you are asked to pay into any other account, that is a serious reason to stop.

Q: Where can I see a project's escrow bank?
A: In the contract and in the Dubai Land Department project registry (data.dubai or DLD Open Data).

Q: Does escrow protect against handover delays?
A: It protects the money, not the timeline. Look for delay compensation in the contract.

## How to choose an off-plan property in Dubai: a 12-point checklist

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/off-plan-checklist/

Twelve things to check before booking an apartment in a building under construction in Dubai. Save the list and run every project on your shortlist through it.

- Checking takes 1–2 hours per project and saves months of trouble.

- Half of the points can be checked with open DLD data.

- Compare projects on the full cost, not the 'from' price.

- Decide only after comparing at least three projects.

### 1–3. Developer and project
1) How many projects the developer has delivered and how late. 2) The project is registered with the DLD and has RERA approval to sell. 3) The completion percentage and planned handover date in the registry match what the seller promises.

### 4–6. Money and protection
4) The project has an escrow account and you pay only into it. 5) The sales agreement (SPA) covers delay compensation and termination terms. 6) You know what happens if you resell before handover: after what share of payments the developer allows assignment and at what fee.

### 7–9. Full cost
7) The price plus the 4% DLD fee, registration fees and agent commission. 8) The service charge per square foot per year — it affects net yield. 9) The payment plan: how much is due before handover and whether there are post-handover payments.

### 10–12. Area and income
10) How many units are being built in the area now — strong future competition for tenants pushes rents down. 11) Real rents from the DLD rental index, not the seller's forecast. 12) Price per square foot against the area average and against ready homes nearby.

### How to use the checklist
Make a table: projects in columns, the twelve points in rows. A project with three or more open questions is better put aside. A great area does not save a weak developer, and a low price does not make up for a bad payment plan.

Q: How many projects should I compare?
A: At least three in the same budget and area — that shows what price and payment plan are normal for the market.

Q: What matters more: the area or the developer?
A: For off-plan, the developer: timelines and quality depend on it. The area drives demand and rent after handover.

Q: Can I check everything myself?
A: Yes, most of it, using open DLD data and the developer's documents. PromptEstates gathers it in one card.

## How to buy off-plan property in Dubai: every step from booking to keys

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/how-to-buy-off-plan/

An off-plan purchase is not one transaction but a chain of 10 steps spread over 2–4 years. Here is each of them: what you sign, what you pay, what to check and where buyers most often go wrong.

- At booking buyers usually pay 5–20% of the price plus the 4% Dubai Land Department fee.

- The sales and purchase agreement (SPA) is signed within about 30 days of booking.

- The deal is registered in the DLD Oqood system and every payment goes to the project escrow account.

- After completion comes the snagging inspection, the final payment and the title deed.

### Step 1. Budget and the full cost
Count the full cost, not the advertised price: the unit price, the 4% DLD fee, the Oqood registration admin fee and, after handover, the title deed fee, the advance service charge and the DEWA deposit. Keep a reserve too: the balance on handover (often 30–60%) is due at once, and banks finance off-plan only to a limited extent and usually close to completion.

### Step 2. Choosing and checking the project
Make sure the project is registered with the Dubai Land Department and has an escrow account — both are visible in the Dubai REST app and the DLD project registry. Look at the developer's record: how many projects it has delivered and how late, plus the current completion percentage and the planned completion date. Compare the price per square metre with ready homes and other new projects in the area.

### Step 3. Booking (EOI and reservation form)
At launch developers often collect expressions of interest (EOI) with a refundable deposit. Once you pick a unit you sign a reservation form and pay a booking deposit — usually 5–10% or a fixed amount. A passport is enough; UAE residency is not required. Get in writing when the booking deposit is refundable.

### Step 4. First instalment and the DLD fee
Usually within a few weeks of booking you top up the first instalment of the plan (most often to 10–20% of the price) and pay the 4% DLD fee. The developer cannot register the deal in Oqood until the fee is paid. Some developers cover the fee as a promotion — this must be stated in the documents.

### Step 5. The sales and purchase agreement (SPA)
The SPA is the key document. Check the exact unit number and area (and the allowed deviation), the finishing specification, the payment plan, the handover date and grace period, compensation for delays, penalties for your late payments, and the termination and assignment terms. If something was promised verbally, ask for it in the contract or an annex.

### Step 6. Oqood registration
Once the SPA is signed and the fee paid, the developer registers the deal in the Dubai Land Department's Oqood system and you receive the Oqood certificate (Initial Contract of Sale). This is your protection: the deal sits in the government registry and the unit cannot be sold twice.

### Step 7. Payments during construction
The remaining instalments follow the schedule — by date or by construction milestone. Money goes only to the project escrow account named in the SPA, never to the developer's or agent's own account. Keep every receipt and statement: you will need them for a resale, a mortgage and the handover.

### Step 8. Selling before handover (assignment)
If your plans change, the unit can be assigned before handover. Developers usually allow this only after a set share of the price has been paid (often 30–40%) and issue a NOC for a fee. The new buyer replaces you in Oqood, and the DLD fee is paid again on the resale.

### Step 9. Completion and snagging
When the building receives its completion certificate, the developer sends a handover notice and the final payment statement. Before you sign the handover, inspect the unit yourself or with a snagging inspector: cracks, plumbing, air conditioning, windows, the area. Every defect goes on the snagging list and the developer must fix it.

### Step 10. Keys and the title deed
You pay the balance (in cash or with a mortgage), settle the service charge and connect DEWA. The developer hands over the keys and the DLD converts the Oqood record into a full title deed in your name. From then on you can rent the home out (the lease is registered in Ejari) or sell it as a ready property.

Q: Can I buy off-plan without UAE residency?
A: Yes. Foreigners buy in freehold areas with a passport; no visa or Emirates ID is needed for the purchase.

Q: Can I buy off-plan remotely?
A: Yes: booking, SPA and payments can be handled remotely, with documents signed electronically or by power of attorney. Pay only into the escrow account named in the contract.

Q: What if the developer delays handover?
A: Go by the SPA: it sets the grace period and compensation. Your money stays in the escrow account, and if a project is cancelled RERA returns it to buyers.

Q: When can I resell before handover?
A: Usually after paying 30–40% of the price and getting the developer's NOC; the assignment terms are in the SPA.

## How to buy resale property in Dubai: a step-by-step guide

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/buying-resale/

On the secondary market you buy a finished home from its owner, and the deal takes weeks, not years. Here is every step — from choosing an agent to the new title deed — and every cost on top of the price.

- A cash deal usually takes 2–4 weeks; with a mortgage, 4–8 weeks.

- The agreement (MOU, Form F) is signed with a 10% deposit held by the brokerage.

- Before the transfer the seller gets a NOC from the developer confirming no dues are outstanding.

- Ownership passes at a DLD Trustee office, and the new title deed is issued the same day.

### Step 1. Budget and costs on top of the price
Besides the price, budget for the 4% Dubai Land Department fee, the Trustee office registration fee (about AED 2,000 + VAT for properties under AED 500,000 and AED 4,000 + VAT above), the agent's commission (usually 2% + VAT), the title deed fee and, with a mortgage, mortgage registration (0.25% of the loan) and the bank valuation. Together this is usually 6–8% on top of the price.

### Step 2. The agent and checking the property
Work with a broker licensed by RERA (the BRN can be checked in Dubai REST); the listing should carry a Trakheesi permit. Ask for a copy of the seller's title deed and check the owner, unit number and area. You sign Form B with your agent; the seller signs Form A with theirs.

### Step 3. Viewing, offer and negotiation
Look at the building as well as the unit: common areas, parking, the service charge (published in the DLD service charge index) and any arrears. Ask whether the unit is tenanted: an existing lease passes to the new owner, and a tenant can only be asked to leave under the tenancy law. Offers are made in writing through the agent.

### Step 4. MOU (Form F) and the 10% deposit
Once the price is agreed, both sides sign a memorandum of understanding at the agent's office — RERA Form F. It sets the price, the transfer date, who pays which fees and the exit terms. The buyer hands over a deposit, usually 10% of the price, as a cheque to the seller; the brokerage holds it until the transfer. If the buyer walks away, the deposit usually goes to the seller; if the seller does, it is returned with compensation.

### Step 5. Mortgage (if needed)
Get a bank pre-approval before you sign the MOU. After the MOU the bank values the property and issues a final offer letter. Non-residents can usually borrow up to 50–60% of the value, residents more. If the seller has a mortgage, their bank issues a liability letter and the loan is paid off from the purchase money on transfer day.

### Step 6. NOC from the developer
The seller requests a No Objection Certificate from the developer or the management company confirming that no service charges are outstanding. The NOC fee is usually AED 500–5,000 and the certificate is valid for a limited time, so it is obtained close to the transfer date.

### Step 7. Transfer at the Trustee office
Both sides (in person or through a power of attorney) meet at a registered DLD Trustee office. The buyer brings manager's cheques: to the seller for the price (less the deposit), for the DLD fee and for the Trustee fee. The office checks the documents, the DLD registers the transfer and the new title deed in the buyer's name is issued electronically the same day.

### Step 8. After the deal
Collect the keys and access cards, move DEWA and any chiller account into your name and register with the building's management company. If you rent the home out, the new lease is registered in Ejari. Owning a home in Dubai can also qualify you for a property-based residence visa — see our visa article for the conditions.

Q: How much do the fees add to the price?
A: Usually 6–8%: the 4% DLD fee, the Trustee fee, the agent's 2% + VAT, the title deed and, with a mortgage, mortgage registration and valuation.

Q: Who pays the DLD fee on a resale?
A: By market practice the buyer does, but the parties can agree otherwise — it is recorded in the MOU (Form F).

Q: Can I buy a home that has a tenant?
A: Yes. The lease passes to the new owner; a tenant can only be asked to leave under the tenancy law, with 12 months' notice served through a notary.

Q: Do I have to attend the transfer in person?
A: No: you can act through a notarised power of attorney (POA) given to a representative in the UAE.

## Freehold areas in Dubai and the UAE: where foreigners can own property

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/freehold-areas/

A foreigner can own an apartment or villa in the UAE outright only in designated areas — freehold zones. Here are those areas in Dubai and the other emirates, and how to check a specific property.

- In Dubai the areas open to foreign ownership were set by Regulation No. 3 of 2006 and have been expanded since.

- Freehold is ownership with no time limit: you can rent the home out, sell it and pass it on.

- Outside freehold zones foreigners can only hold long leases or usufruct rights (leasehold).

- An area's status is shown on the title deed or in the Dubai Land Department registry.

### Freehold vs leasehold
Freehold is full ownership with no time limit of the apartment or villa, and in some projects of the land beneath it. Leasehold is the right to hold and use a property for a long term (usually up to 99 years), after which it returns to the landowner. For foreigners in Dubai the main format is freehold in designated areas; outside them deals are possible only as leasehold or usufruct.

### Main freehold areas in Dubai
City centre and business districts: Downtown Dubai, Business Bay, DIFC, City Walk. Waterfront: Dubai Marina, JBR, Palm Jumeirah, Bluewaters, Dubai Islands, Dubai Harbour, La Mer. New communities: Dubai Hills Estate, Dubai Creek Harbour, MBR City and Meydan, JVC, JVT, JLT, Arjan, Al Furjan, Dubai Sports City, Motor City, Town Square, Dubai South. Villa communities: Arabian Ranches, Emirates Hills, The Springs and The Meadows, DAMAC Hills, Jumeirah Golf Estates, Tilal Al Ghaf.

### How to check a property is freehold
For a ready property the ownership type is on the title deed; for one under construction, in the Oqood registration. The project and developer can be found in the Dubai REST app and the DLD project registry. If an agent offers a property outside the well-known areas, ask for written confirmation of the ownership type before paying a deposit.

### Abu Dhabi
In Abu Dhabi foreigners buy in investment zones: Saadiyat Island, Yas Island, Al Reem Island, Al Raha Beach, Al Maryah Island, Masdar City, Al Reef and others. Since 2019 these zones allow full freehold ownership, registered with the Abu Dhabi Real Estate Centre (ADREC).

### Sharjah, Ajman and Ras Al Khaimah
In Sharjah, since 2022 foreigners can own homes in specific projects approved by the emirate, such as Aljada and Maryam Island; elsewhere usufruct rights are available. Ajman has freehold areas in Al Zorah, Emirates City and several waterfront projects. In Ras Al Khaimah: Al Marjan Island, Al Hamra Village and Mina Al Arab. Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah have fewer zones — check the conditions with the emirate's land department.

### What freehold ownership gives you
The home is registered in your name; you can rent it out, sell it, mortgage it with a UAE bank and pass it on to heirs. Owning property can also qualify you for a residence visa: the two-year investor visa, or the Golden Visa for property worth AED 2 million or more. Since April 2026 the two-year visa has no minimum property value for the sole owner of a ready home.

Q: Can a foreigner buy outside a freehold area?
A: In Dubai only as a long lease or usufruct right (leasehold), not as ownership.

Q: Do I need a residence visa to buy in a freehold area?
A: No. A passport is enough, and the purchase can be completed remotely.

Q: Can the home be inherited?
A: Yes. To make sure it passes according to your wishes, register a will, for example with DIFC Wills.

## UAE retirement visa: how to move to Dubai after 55

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/retirement-visa/

The UAE issues a dedicated residence visa for retirees: five years, no employer or sponsor, renewable. Here is who qualifies, which financial condition you need to meet and how to apply.

- Age 55 or over; the visa is issued for five years and can be renewed.

- You need to meet one financial condition: savings, property or regular income.

- Health insurance valid in the UAE is mandatory.

- A spouse and children can be included.

### Who it is for
The retirement visa is for foreigners aged 55 or over who want to live in the UAE without a job or a local sponsor. It is open both to people who have worked in the UAE for years and are retiring, and to those moving from abroad. Employment is not required or expected.

### Financial conditions
Meeting one of them is enough. According to official UAE portals in 2026: property in the UAE worth at least AED 1 million, or savings of at least AED 1 million in a UAE bank, or a regular income (pension, annuity) of at least AED 20,000 a month; for people who have worked in the UAE for 15 years or more the income threshold is lower, around AED 15,000. Exact amounts and permitted combinations vary by emirate, so check with ICP or GDRFA when you apply.

### Retirement visa through property
If you choose the property route, the home must be in your name and registered with the emirate's land department; its value is confirmed by a valuation. Usually this means a ready property without an outstanding mortgage — check the requirements for your case. It suits people who plan to buy a home to live in anyway: the purchase becomes the basis for the visa.

### Documents
A passport valid for at least six months, a photo, proof of the financial condition (a bank deposit statement, the title deed and valuation, or a pension certificate and statements showing it is paid), and health insurance valid in the UAE. Documents issued abroad usually need to be attested and translated into Arabic.

### How to apply
In Dubai through GDRFA (the Retire in Dubai programme), or through ICP for the other emirates. The process is the usual one for residence visas: application and fees, an entry permit if you are not yet in the country, a medical test, biometrics and the Emirates ID. It usually takes a few weeks.

### Family and renewal
A spouse and children can be added; each has a medical test and gets their own Emirates ID. After five years the visa is renewed if the financial condition is still met. If you sell the property or your savings drop below the threshold, the basis for the visa no longer exists.

### Retirement visa or Golden Visa
If you are 55+ and your budget for a home is AED 1–2 million, the retirement visa is often simpler: the threshold is lower than the Golden Visa through property (AED 2 million and up). If you buy for more than AED 2 million, the Golden Visa gives a longer term (usually 10 years) and does not depend on age.

Q: From what age is the retirement visa available?
A: From 55. You do not need to have worked in the UAE — it is also issued to people moving from abroad.

Q: Can I work on a retirement visa?
A: It is not meant for employment. To work you need a work visa or another basis.

Q: Does a mortgaged home qualify?
A: The retirement visa usually expects a property without an outstanding mortgage — check with GDRFA or ICP for your case.

Q: Do I have to live in the UAE full time?
A: UAE residence visas other than the Golden Visa can lapse after a long absence (usually over six months), so keep an eye on the dates.

## UAE visa through financial investment: fund, business and bank deposit

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/investment-visa-deposit/

The Golden Visa can be obtained not only through property but also through financial investment — a deposit in an investment fund or capital in a UAE company. Here are the options, thresholds and documents, and how they differ from a regular bank deposit.

- The investor Golden Visa is issued for 10 years for investments of AED 2 million or more.

- Fund route: a deposit of at least AED 2 million in an accredited UAE investment fund.

- Business route: a company or a share in one with capital of AED 2 million or more.

- A regular bank deposit on its own does not give a Golden Visa, but can support a retirement visa (55+).

### Which financial investments qualify
According to the official UAE portal, the investor Golden Visa (usually for 10 years) is issued to people who have deposited at least AED 2 million in an investment fund in the UAE; who own a UAE company with capital of AED 2 million or a share in one worth that much; or who pay at least AED 250,000 a year in taxes and fees to the government. The investment must be your own money, not a loan.

### Deposit in an investment fund
This is the most 'financial' route: you place AED 2 million or more in a fund registered in the UAE and receive a letter from the fund confirming the amount and term. The fund must be accredited for Golden Visa purposes — check the list and the letter requirements with ICP or GDRFA. The money usually has to stay in the fund for the whole visa term: withdrawing below the threshold removes the basis for renewal.

### Company capital
If you set up a business in the UAE or buy a share, the basis is capital of AED 2 million or more, confirmed by the founding documents and trade licence. With several partners, each partner's share counts. This route suits entrepreneurs who plan to operate in the UAE anyway.

### What about simply putting money in a bank
A regular fixed deposit in a UAE bank does not count towards the Golden Visa on its own. But savings of AED 1 million or more in a UAE bank are one of the grounds for the five-year retirement visa if you are 55 or over. Before placing the money, ask the bank whether it issues a deposit confirmation for visa purposes and for how long the funds must be locked.

### Documents and process
A passport, photo, the fund's letter or the company documents (licence, articles, proof of capital), statements showing the source of funds, and health insurance. You apply through ICP, or GDRFA in Dubai; then come the medical test, biometrics and the Emirates ID. A spouse and children can be included.

### Fund, business or property
Investing AED 2 million or more in property gives the same Golden Visa, but the asset can be rented out for income and its value is confirmed by a DLD valuation. A fund is easier to manage, but returns and risks depend on its strategy. A business makes sense if you really operate in the UAE. If your budget is under AED 2 million, look at the two-year visa for a ready home.

Q: Can I get a Golden Visa for a bank deposit?
A: A regular bank deposit does not count on its own. You need AED 2 million in an accredited investment fund or company capital. Savings of AED 1 million in a bank qualify for the retirement visa (55+).

Q: Can I invest borrowed money?
A: No, for the investor Golden Visa the investment must be your own funds.

Q: What if I withdraw money from the fund?
A: If the investment drops below AED 2 million, the basis for the visa disappears and it cannot be renewed.

Q: Can I combine a fund and property?
A: Each basis is assessed on its own terms; whether different investments can be combined should be checked with ICP when you apply.

## UAE residency through investment: all the options compared

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/uae-residency-options/

The UAE has no single 'investor visa' — there are several programmes with different thresholds and conditions. We put them side by side: how much you need to invest, how long the visa lasts, whether off-plan counts and whether family can be included.

- Two-year visa for a ready home in Dubai: since 2026 no minimum value for a sole owner.

- Golden Visa through property — from AED 2 million, usually for 10 years, off-plan counts.

- Golden Visa through a fund or business — investments from AED 2 million.

- Retirement visa for 55+ — AED 1 million in savings or property, or a regular income.

### Two-year investor visa through property
The basis is a ready home in Dubai with a title deed. Since April 2026 there is no minimum property value for a sole owner; joint owners need at least AED 400,000 per share. Off-plan does not qualify until handover. The visa is renewed every two years while you own the property, and family can be included. Details in our article on the two-year visa.

### Golden Visa through property
The threshold is AED 2 million by the land department's valuation; several properties can be combined. Off-plan from approved developers and mortgaged property (with a NOC from a UAE bank) qualify. The term is usually 10 years and you do not have to live in the UAE full time. Details in our Golden Visa article.

### Golden Visa through a fund or business
AED 2 million or more in an accredited UAE investment fund, or a company or share with capital of AED 2 million or more, or AED 250,000 or more a year in taxes and fees. The term is usually 10 years too. It suits people who do not want to own property or who run a business in the UAE.

### Retirement visa (55+)
For people aged 55 or over: one condition among savings of AED 1 million in a UAE bank, property worth AED 1 million, or a regular income of AED 20,000 a month (lower for those who have worked in the UAE for 15+ years). Five years, renewable.

### How to choose
Budget under AED 2 million and a ready home — the two-year visa. Buying for AED 2 million or more, including off-plan — the Golden Visa through property. Do not want to buy a home — the Golden Visa through a fund or business. Aged 55+ with savings or a home worth AED 1 million — the retirement visa. In every case the rules change, so check with ICP, GDRFA or the DLD when you apply.

### What all the options share
A medical test, biometrics and the Emirates ID; health insurance; the right to include a spouse and children; and the basis must be kept for the whole visa term — if you sell the property or withdraw funds below the threshold, you cannot renew. None of these visas needs a local sponsor or employer.

Q: Which visa is cheapest through property?
A: The two-year visa for a ready home in Dubai: since April 2026 there is no minimum value for a sole owner.

Q: Which visa works with off-plan?
A: The Golden Visa: off-plan from an approved developer valued at AED 2 million or more qualifies. The two-year visa needs a ready home.

Q: Can I get UAE citizenship through investment?
A: No. All these programmes give residency, not citizenship.

## Property revaluation for the Golden Visa: if you bought below AED 2 million

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/golden-visa-valuation/

For a Golden Visa through property, what counts is not the price you paid but the property's value in an official valuation on the date you apply. If your home has gone up and is now worth AED 2 million or more, a revaluation can open the way to the visa.

- The Golden Visa threshold is AED 2 million by the land department's valuation certificate, not the contract price.

- Example: an apartment bought for AED 1.7 million is now worth about AED 2.2 million — by valuation it clears the threshold.

- The valuation is done by a valuer accredited with the Dubai Land Department and ordered through DLD services.

- The result is not guaranteed: the valuer relies on actual sales in the building and area.

### Why the valuation matters, not the purchase price
When you apply for a Golden Visa through property in Dubai, the property's value is confirmed by a Dubai Land Department valuation certificate. The price in the sales contract is only a starting point: if the market has risen, today's valuation can be noticeably higher. So an owner who bought below AED 2 million does not necessarily lose the right to the visa.

### Example: AED 1.7 million → 2.2 million
A client bought an apartment for AED 1,700,000. Similar apartments in the same building have recently sold for AED 2.1–2.3 million. If an accredited valuer values the apartment at AED 2,200,000, the certificate confirms a value above the threshold and the client can apply for the Golden Visa on that basis. If the valuation comes in at AED 1.95 million, the threshold is not met and another option is needed.

### How to order a revaluation
The valuation is carried out by a valuer accredited with the DLD. You apply through Dubai Land Department services — the website, the Dubai REST app or service centres. Usually you need the title deed, the owner's passport and access to the home for an inspection. It is a paid service; check the cost and timing when you order. The certificate is valid for a limited time, so apply for the visa soon after the valuation.

### What the valuer looks at
Above all, prices of actual sales of similar properties in the same building and area over recent months (DLD data). Area, floor, view, condition and finishing, and parking are also taken into account. Before ordering, look at recent sales yourself: if similar apartments sell for under AED 2 million, a revaluation is unlikely to reach the amount you need.

### Mortgages, off-plan and several properties
