A mortgaged property qualifies: you need a valuation of AED 2 million or more and a no-objection letter (NOC) from a UAE bank. For a property under construction the value may be determined differently — based on the contract price and the developer's statement; check before applying. If you own several properties, their valuations can be added together to reach AED 2 million.

### If the valuation falls short
Options: buy another property and combine the values; wait for the market to rise and repeat the valuation later; or apply for the two-year investor visa — since 2026 a sole owner of a ready home in Dubai faces no minimum value. If the property is in another emirate, that emirate's land department does the valuation.

Q: Can I get a Golden Visa if I bought below AED 2 million?
A: Yes, if the property's current DLD valuation is AED 2 million or more. The value on the date of application counts, not the purchase price.

Q: Who carries out the valuation?
A: A valuer accredited with the Dubai Land Department, ordered through DLD services.

Q: How long is the valuation certificate valid?
A: For a limited time — apply for the visa soon after the valuation. Check the exact period when you order.

Q: Can a mortgaged apartment be revalued?
A: Yes. For the visa you need a valuation of AED 2 million or more and a NOC from a UAE bank.

## UAE mortgages for foreigners: how much you can borrow and how

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/uae-mortgage-foreigners/

Foreigners can take a mortgage from a UAE bank — both residents and people living abroad. Here are the Central Bank limits, the down payment, income requirements, every fee and what is different for off-plan.

- A resident expat buying a first home under AED 5 million can borrow up to 80% — a down payment from 20%.

- Banks usually lend non-residents 50–60% of the value.

- For property under construction the limit is lower — usually no more than 50%.

- Repayments on all loans must not exceed 50% of income.

### Who can get a mortgage
UAE mortgages are available both to residents with a visa and Emirates ID and to non-residents living abroad. Residents have a wider choice of banks and terms; not every bank lends to non-residents, and usually with a bigger down payment. The property must be in an area where foreigners may own property.

### UAE Central Bank limits
Central Bank rules cap the loan-to-value ratio. For resident expats: a first home up to AED 5 million — up to 80% of the value, above AED 5 million — up to 70%, second and further properties — up to 60%. For property under construction — up to 50%. Banks usually lend non-residents 50–60%. The exact percentage depends on the bank, your income and the property.

### Borrower requirements
Monthly repayments on all loans must not exceed 50% of income. The term is up to 25 years, and at the end of it the borrower should usually be no older than 65 (salaried) or 70 (self-employed). Banks look at income stability, credit history (in the UAE, the AECB report) and a minimum salary that differs from bank to bank.

### Documents
A passport; for residents, the visa and Emirates ID; a salary certificate or business income documents; six months of bank statements; and a credit report. Non-residents usually need statements and proof of income from their country of residence, sometimes a credit report from there too. After pre-approval the bank values the property and issues the final offer.

### Every mortgage fee
Besides the down payment and the usual purchase costs (the 4% DLD fee and others), budget for: mortgage registration at the DLD — 0.25% of the loan plus an admin fee; the bank's arrangement fee (usually up to 1% of the loan); the property valuation (a few thousand AED); and life and property insurance. Under Central Bank rules the early repayment fee is capped at 1% of the outstanding balance, up to AED 10,000.

### Fixed or variable rate
Banks offer a fixed rate for the first 1–5 years, after which it becomes variable and is linked to EIBOR, the UAE interbank rate. Compare not only the rate but also what it becomes after the fixed period, the fees and the early repayment terms.

### Mortgages for off-plan
Banks lend cautiously on property under construction: the limit is usually up to 50%, and they more often finance close to handover, when the property is nearly ready. So plan an off-plan payment schedule so that you cover most of it before handover from your own funds and take the mortgage for the balance when you get the keys.

Q: Can a non-resident get a mortgage in the UAE?
A: Yes, but not from every bank and usually for 50–60% of the property's value.

Q: What is the minimum down payment?
A: For a resident expat buying a first home up to AED 5 million — 20%; more for expensive homes, second homes and off-plan.

Q: Can I get a Golden Visa if the home is mortgaged?
A: Yes, if the property is valued at AED 2 million or more and a UAE bank has issued a NOC.

Q: How much does early repayment cost?
A: Under Central Bank rules — no more than 1% of the outstanding balance and no more than AED 10,000.

## Property taxes in the UAE: what an apartment owner pays

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/uae-property-taxes/

The UAE has no annual property tax, and individuals pay no tax on rental income or capital gains. But there are fees — one-off at purchase and regular ones for upkeep. Here are all of them, plus the one people often forget: taxes in the country where you are tax resident.

- There is no annual property tax for private owners.

- An individual's rental income and profit on sale are not taxed in the UAE.

- The main one-off cost at purchase is the 4% Dubai Land Department fee.

- Regular costs are the building service charge and the municipality housing fee.

### One-off payments at purchase
The main one is the Dubai Land Department fee of 4% of the price. On top come admin fees for registration (Oqood for off-plan, the Trustee office for resale) and for issuing the title deed, the agent's commission on resale (usually 2% + VAT) and, with a mortgage, mortgage registration at 0.25% of the loan. A detailed breakdown is in our article on buying costs.

### An owner's annual costs
There is no property tax, but there is the building service charge — calculated per square foot and published in the DLD index. There is also the Dubai Municipality housing fee: it is added to the DEWA bills of whoever lives in the home and for a tenant equals 5% of the annual rent. Add utilities and, optionally, insurance.

### Tax on rental income
Individuals in the UAE pay no tax on rental income. The 9% corporate tax introduced in 2023 applies to businesses; under its rules an individual's income from renting out their own property is not a business activity unless it requires a licence. If you own through a company, different rules apply — get advice from a tax specialist.

### Tax on sale
There is no capital gains tax for individuals: profit on selling an apartment in the UAE is not taxed. When selling you only pay related costs — for example the developer's NOC and the agent's commission if you used one. By market practice the 4% DLD fee is paid by the buyer.

### VAT
Sales and leases of residential property in the UAE are mostly exempt from VAT, and the first sale of a new home is zero-rated. 5% VAT applies to commercial property and to services around the deal — the agent's commission, Trustee fees and some management company services.

### Inheritance
There is no inheritance tax in the UAE. But who receives the home matters: to make sure it passes according to your wishes, a foreigner should register a will — for example with DIFC Wills or the Dubai courts. Without a will the process is longer and more complex.

### Taxes in your home country
No taxes in the UAE does not mean no taxes at all: if you are tax resident elsewhere, that country may tax rental income and gains on UAE property. Much depends on the double tax treaty and on whether you become UAE tax resident. Before buying, it is worth consulting a tax specialist in your own country.

Q: Is there a property tax in Dubai?
A: There is no annual property tax for private owners. There is the one-off 4% DLD fee at purchase, the building service charge and the municipality housing fee.

Q: Do I pay tax on renting out my apartment?
A: Not in the UAE if you rent out as an individual. But the country where you are tax resident may tax it.

Q: Is selling an apartment taxed?
A: There is no capital gains tax for individuals in the UAE.

Q: Is VAT charged when buying a home?
A: Residential sales are mostly VAT-exempt; 5% applies to the agent's commission and some related services.

## Dubai off-plan market in numbers

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/guide/dubai-market-data/

A summary table of 14 Dubai areas built on official open data from the Dubai Land Department (DLD): actual sales transactions over the last 12 months and the registry of projects under construction. The data is refreshed with every new DLD export.

- Source: Dubai Land Department open data on the data.dubai portal.

- Prices are medians of registered sales over 12 months, not advertised prices.

- For each area: price per m², studio, 1 and 2 bedrooms, off-plan share, projects under construction and past their handover date.

- The table can be downloaded as CSV and quoted with a link to this page.

### How we calculate
We take the DLD Real Estate Transactions export and keep sales over the last 12 months. The median is the middle of the range: half of the deals are cheaper, half are more expensive, so a few expensive penthouses do not skew it. Apartment prices are medians of unit sales with the given number of bedrooms. The three-year change compares the median price per m² of the first year in the series with the current year.

### Limitations
The median also reflects what is being sold: if an area launches a lot of new, pricier off-plan stock, the median rises faster than the price of any given apartment. This is not a valuation of your home and not investment advice. Area boundaries follow DLD master projects and zones.

### How to cite
Credit the source as “PromptEstates, based on Dubai Land Department data” with the export date shown in the table. If you use the CSV, keep a link to this page.

Q: Where do these numbers come from?
A: From Dubai Land Department open data: the Real Estate Transactions export and the Projects registry on the data.dubai portal.

Q: How often is the table updated?
A: With every new DLD export; the data date is shown under the table.

Q: Can I use the data in my article?
A: Yes, with credit: “PromptEstates, based on Dubai Land Department data” and a link to this page.

## Dubai Marina: off-plan property and the area

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/areas/dubai-marina/

Dubai Marina is one of Dubai’s best-known residential districts: high-rise towers around a man-made canal with a promenade and yachts, minutes from JBR beach.

- Waterfront residential towers, mostly apartments.

- Next to JBR beach and the Marina Walk promenade.

- Served by metro and tram.

- In demand with tenants, including short-term rentals.

### What the area is like
The district is built around a canal about three kilometres long. It is full of restaurants, shops and walking areas, and the beach is within walking distance.

### Who it suits
People who want to live by the water in a lively place, and investors counting on rental income: demand for apartments here is consistently strong.

### Transport
The area has metro stations and a tram line linking Dubai Marina with JBR and Palm Jumeirah. Sheikh Zayed Road runs alongside.

### What homes are sold here
Mostly apartments in high-rise towers, from studios to penthouses. Free plots are scarce, so there are fewer off-plan projects than in developing areas.

Q: How much does a square metre cost in Dubai Marina?
A: According to the Dubai Land Department (DLD), the median sale price in Dubai Marina over the last 12 months is AED 21,648 per m² (data as of 2026-10-03). In 2023 the median was AED 16,181 per m².

Q: How much is an apartment in Dubai Marina?
A: Median DLD transaction prices over 12 months in Dubai Marina: studio — AED 920,000, 1 bedroom — AED 1,680,000, 2 bedrooms — AED 2,550,000. This is the median across all deals in the area, not a valuation of a specific unit.

Q: What share of deals in Dubai Marina are off-plan?
A: 7% of sales in Dubai Marina over the last 12 months were off-plan purchases, according to DLD data.

Q: Is Dubai Marina good for renting out?
A: The area is popular with tenants, including tourists. Compare a specific unit’s yield with the area average.

Q: How far is the beach?
A: JBR beach is within walking distance of most of the area.

## Business Bay: off-plan property and the area

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/areas/business-bay/

Business Bay is a central Dubai district along the Dubai Canal, next to Downtown, Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall.

- A mix of office and residential towers.

- Next to Downtown Dubai and Burj Khalifa.

- A promenade along the Dubai Canal.

- Has a metro station.

### What the area is like
It is one of the city’s main business quarters, and many residential developments have appeared here in recent years. Most parts of Dubai are quick to reach from it.

### Who it suits
People who work in the centre and want to live nearby, and investors who value a central location and tenant demand.

### Transport
The Business Bay metro station is nearby, along with Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road. Downtown Dubai is a walk away along the canal promenade.

### What homes are sold here
Apartments in high-rise residential towers, including ones with canal and Burj Khalifa views. There are many new projects.

Q: How much does a square metre cost in Business Bay?
A: According to the Dubai Land Department (DLD), the median sale price in Business Bay over the last 12 months is AED 26,838 per m² (data as of 2026-10-03). In 2023 the median was AED 22,242 per m².

Q: How much is an apartment in Business Bay?
A: Median DLD transaction prices over 12 months in Business Bay: studio — AED 1,120,000, 1 bedroom — AED 2,000,000, 2 bedrooms — AED 3,090,000. This is the median across all deals in the area, not a valuation of a specific unit.

Q: What share of deals in Business Bay are off-plan?
A: 54% of sales in Business Bay over the last 12 months were off-plan purchases, according to DLD data.

Q: Who is Business Bay for?
A: People who work in the centre, and investors counting on renting to professionals.

Q: Is the area noisy?
A: It is a busy business district; homes on the canal promenade are usually quieter than those by the main roads.

## JVC: off-plan property and the area

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/areas/jvc/

Jumeirah Village Circle (JVC) is a residential community with low- and mid-rise buildings, parks and a wide choice of apartments, townhouses and villas.

- Apartments, townhouses and villas.

- Plenty of parks and green space.

- A lower entry price than waterfront districts.

- Many new projects from different developers.

### What the area is like
JVC is laid out as a circle of residential clusters and community parks. It has a shopping mall, schools and nurseries.

### Who it suits
Families looking for a quiet area, and investors on a moderate budget: the entry price is lower here than by the water.

### Transport
The area lies between Al Khail Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road; getting around is mainly by car.

### What homes are sold here
Apartments in low- and mid-rise buildings, townhouses and villas. There are many new projects from different developers.

Q: Why do investors choose JVC?

Q: Are there schools in the area?

## Dubai Hills Estate: off-plan property and the area

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/areas/dubai-hills/

Dubai Hills Estate is a large residential community with a park, a golf course and its own mall, between Downtown and Dubai Marina.

- Apartments, townhouses and villas.

- A large park and an 18-hole golf course.

- Dubai Hills Mall.

- Geared to families.

### What the area is like
It is a master-planned community with green spaces, schools and clinics, conveniently placed for both the city centre and the coast.

### Who it suits
Families who want greenery and amenities close to home, and people buying a home to live in for the long term.

### Transport
The area sits by Al Khail Road and Umm Suqeim Street; Downtown Dubai and Dubai Marina are an easy drive away.

### What homes are sold here
Apartments in complexes by the park and the mall, townhouses and villas, including by the golf course. The community is a joint venture of Emaar and Meraas.

Q: How much does a square metre cost in Dubai Hills Estate?

A: Median DLD transaction prices over 12 months in Dubai Hills Estate: studio — AED 970,000, 1 bedroom — AED 1,730,000, 2 bedrooms — AED 2,690,000. This is the median across all deals in the area, not a valuation of a specific unit.

Q: What share of deals in Dubai Hills Estate are off-plan?
A: 52% of sales in Dubai Hills Estate over the last 12 months were off-plan purchases, according to DLD data.

Q: Who is the developer of Dubai Hills Estate?
A: The community is a joint venture of Emaar and Meraas.

Q: Is the area good for families?
A: Yes: there is plenty of greenery, schools and a large park.

## Dubai Creek Harbour: off-plan property and the area

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/areas/dubai-creek-harbour/

Dubai Creek Harbour is a new district on the shore of Dubai Creek with a promenade, a marina and views of the Downtown skyline.

- Waterfront residential towers.

- A promenade and a yacht marina.

- Next to the Ras Al Khor wildlife sanctuary.

- Views of Downtown and Burj Khalifa.

### What the area is like
The district is being built as a single master plan with parks and walking areas along the water. Most homes here are new apartments.

### Who it suits
People who want to live by the water in a calmer setting than Dubai Marina, and buyers looking for new homes in a developing area.

### Transport
The area is close to Dubai International Airport and Ras Al Khor Road; Downtown Dubai is an easy drive away.

### What homes are sold here
Apartments in new waterfront residential towers, often with Downtown views. The district is developed by Emaar.

Q: How much does a square metre cost in Dubai Creek Harbour?
A: According to the Dubai Land Department (DLD), the median sale price in Dubai Creek Harbour over the last 12 months is AED 27,692 per m² (data as of 2026-10-03). In 2023 the median was AED 22,350 per m².

Q: How much is an apartment in Dubai Creek Harbour?
A: Median DLD transaction prices over 12 months in Dubai Creek Harbour: 1 bedroom — AED 1,960,000, 2 bedrooms — AED 3,180,000. This is the median across all deals in the area, not a valuation of a specific unit.

Q: What share of deals in Dubai Creek Harbour are off-plan?
A: 67% of sales in Dubai Creek Harbour over the last 12 months were off-plan purchases, according to DLD data.

Q: Who is the developer?
A: Dubai Creek Harbour is developed by Emaar.

Q: How far is the airport?
A: Dubai International Airport is close by — one of the area’s advantages.

## Palm Jumeirah: off-plan property and the area

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/areas/palm-jumeirah/

Palm Jumeirah is a palm-shaped man-made island and one of Dubai’s most recognisable addresses, with beachfront residences, villas and hotels.

- Beachfront apartments and villas.

- The premium end of the market.

- Resort hotels and restaurants.

- Many developments have their own beaches.

### What the area is like
The island is made up of a trunk lined with residential buildings and fronds lined with villas. It is home to well-known hotels and beach clubs.

### Who it suits
Buyers of premium homes by the sea, and investors counting on rentals at the top end of the market.

### Transport
A monorail runs along the island’s trunk; the island connects to the mainland near Sheikh Zayed Road, and to the outer crescent by an undersea tunnel.

### What homes are sold here
Apartments in residences on the trunk and crescent, villas on the fronds. New projects are most often branded beachfront residences.

Q: How much does a square metre cost in Palm Jumeirah?
A: According to the Dubai Land Department (DLD), the median sale price in Palm Jumeirah over the last 12 months is AED 36,916 per m² (data as of 2026-10-03). In 2023 the median was AED 28,637 per m².

Q: How much is an apartment in Palm Jumeirah?
A: Median DLD transaction prices over 12 months in Palm Jumeirah: studio — AED 1,370,000, 1 bedroom — AED 3,510,000, 2 bedrooms — AED 5,810,000. This is the median across all deals in the area, not a valuation of a specific unit.

Q: What share of deals in Palm Jumeirah are off-plan?
A: 31% of sales in Palm Jumeirah over the last 12 months were off-plan purchases, according to DLD data.

Q: Who is the developer of the island?
A: Palm Jumeirah was created by Nakheel.

Q: Is the island good for renting out?
A: Demand is strong in the premium segment, including holiday lets; the entry price is high too.

## Downtown Dubai: off-plan property and the area

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/areas/downtown-dubai/

Downtown Dubai is the city's business and tourist centre around Burj Khalifa, Dubai Mall and the Dubai Fountain. The district's main developer is Emaar.

- Burj Khalifa, Dubai Mall, Dubai Opera and the fountain within walking distance.

- Burj Khalifa / Dubai Mall metro station.

- Mostly apartments in high-rise towers.

- One of the most expensive areas per square metre.

### What the area is like
Emaar planned Downtown as the city centre: Mohammed Bin Rashid Boulevard, residential towers, hotels, restaurants and Dubai's main landmarks in a compact area.

### Who it suits
People who want to live centrally and walk, and investors interested in tourist demand for short-term rentals. The entry price is higher than in most areas.

### Transport
Burj Khalifa / Dubai Mall station on the Red Line and direct access to Sheikh Zayed Road. Many places in the area are walkable.

### What homes are sold here
Apartments from studios to penthouses in high-rise towers, including branded residences. New projects appear less often than in developing areas.

Q: How much does a square metre cost in Downtown Dubai?
A: According to the Dubai Land Department (DLD), the median sale price in Downtown Dubai over the last 12 months is AED 33,742 per m² (data as of 2026-10-03). In 2023 the median was AED 29,759 per m².

Q: How much is an apartment in Downtown Dubai?
A: Median DLD transaction prices over 12 months in Downtown Dubai: studio — AED 1,780,000, 1 bedroom — AED 2,350,000, 2 bedrooms — AED 3,900,000. This is the median across all deals in the area, not a valuation of a specific unit.

Q: What share of deals in Downtown Dubai are off-plan?
A: 37% of sales in Downtown Dubai over the last 12 months were off-plan purchases, according to DLD data.

Q: Is Downtown good for short-term rental?
A: The area is popular with tourists, so short-term rental demand is high. Check holiday-home rules with DET and the building's management.

Q: Can you get a Golden Visa here?
A: Yes, apartments from AED 2 million — the Golden Visa threshold — are common here.

## MBR City and Meydan: off-plan property and the area

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/areas/mbr-city/

Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum City (MBR City) is a large district between Downtown and Ras Al Khor. It includes Meydan, Sobha Hartland, District One and complexes on the Dubai Canal.

- A 10–15-minute drive to Downtown.

- Villas with lagoons, townhouses and apartments.

- The Meydan racecourse and plenty of green space.

- Developers include Sobha, Meydan, Azizi, Ellington and others.

### What the area is like
MBR City brings together several communities: Sobha Hartland with villas and apartments among greenery, District One with a crystal lagoon, Meydan with its racecourse and Azizi Riviera along the Dubai Canal.

### Who it suits
Families who want a villa or a large apartment close to the centre, and investors counting on the area's growth as it is built out.

### Transport
The area borders Al Khail Road and Meydan Road; Downtown and Business Bay are a 10–15-minute drive away. Most of the area has no metro.

### What homes are sold here
Villas and townhouses by lagoons and parks, as well as apartments in Sobha Hartland, Meydan and along the Dubai Canal.

Q: How much does a square metre cost in MBR City & Meydan?
A: According to the Dubai Land Department (DLD), the median sale price in MBR City & Meydan over the last 12 months is AED 21,337 per m² (data as of 2026-10-03). In 2023 the median was AED 20,956 per m².

Q: How much is an apartment in MBR City & Meydan?
A: Median DLD transaction prices over 12 months in MBR City & Meydan: studio — AED 800,000, 1 bedroom — AED 1,400,000, 2 bedrooms — AED 2,360,000. This is the median across all deals in the area, not a valuation of a specific unit.

Q: What share of deals in MBR City & Meydan are off-plan?
A: 35% of sales in MBR City & Meydan over the last 12 months were off-plan purchases, according to DLD data.

Q: How does MBR City differ from Dubai Hills?
A: Both are green and family-oriented, but MBR City is closer to Downtown and includes several different communities with lagoons.

Q: Are there many off-plan projects here?
A: Yes, the area is still being built out, with many projects under construction from different developers.

## Dubai South: off-plan property and the area

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/areas/dubai-south/

Dubai South is a large district in the south of Dubai around Al Maktoum International Airport (DWC) and Expo City Dubai. DWC is planned to be expanded into the city's main airport.

- Al Maktoum airport and Expo City Dubai nearby.

- One of the lowest entry prices in Dubai.

- Large projects: Emaar South, Azizi Venice.

- The area is still being actively built.

### What the area is like
Dubai South is conceived as a city around the airport: residential communities, a logistics zone and business parks. Next to it is the former Expo 2020 site, now Expo City Dubai.

### Who it suits
Investors buying for the area's future development and the airport expansion, and buyers who need a low entry price. Keep in mind it is far from central Dubai.

### Transport
The area is by Emirates Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road; Expo 2020 metro station on the Route 2020 line is a few minutes away. Downtown is about a 40-minute drive.

### What homes are sold here
Apartments, townhouses and villas in large communities, including Emaar South and Azizi Venice. Many projects come with long payment plans.

Q: How much does a square metre cost in Dubai South?
A: According to the Dubai Land Department (DLD), the median sale price in Dubai South over the last 12 months is AED 17,499 per m² (data as of 2026-10-03). In 2023 the median was AED 11,061 per m².

Q: How much is an apartment in Dubai South?
A: Median DLD transaction prices over 12 months in Dubai South: studio — AED 650,000, 1 bedroom — AED 1,150,000, 2 bedrooms — AED 1,680,000. This is the median across all deals in the area, not a valuation of a specific unit.

Q: What share of deals in Dubai South are off-plan?
A: 91% of sales in Dubai South over the last 12 months were off-plan purchases, according to DLD data.

Q: Why do investors look at Dubai South?
A: Because of the low entry price and plans to expand Al Maktoum airport, which may raise demand for housing nearby.

Q: What are the risks?
A: The area is far from the centre and still being built, so rental demand is lower than in established areas for now. Check the developer and handover dates carefully.

## Dubai Islands: off-plan property and the area

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/areas/dubai-islands/

Dubai Islands (formerly Deira Islands) are five man-made islands off the Deira coast developed by Nakheel. Beach resorts, marinas and waterfront residences are being built here.

- Five islands off Deira, the old part of Dubai.

- Master developer: Nakheel.

- Beaches, marinas and resort hotels.

- A noticeably lower entry price than Palm Jumeirah.

### What the area is like
The islands are linked to Deira by bridges and designed for waterfront living: beaches, promenades, yacht marinas and hotels. Most residential projects are still under construction.

### Who it suits
Buyers who want a seaside apartment for less than on Palm Jumeirah or in Dubai Marina, and investors buying at an early stage of the area's development.

### Transport
The islands are linked by bridges to Deira, and Infinity Bridge leads to Bur Dubai. DXB airport is about a 15–20-minute drive.

### What homes are sold here
Apartments and penthouses in low- and mid-rise beachfront complexes, as well as villas. Most projects are under construction.

Q: How much does a square metre cost in Dubai Islands?
A: According to the Dubai Land Department (DLD), the median sale price in Dubai Islands over the last 12 months is AED 29,520 per m² (data as of 2026-10-03). In 2023 the median was AED 25,864 per m².

Q: How much is an apartment in Dubai Islands?
A: Median DLD transaction prices over 12 months in Dubai Islands: studio — AED 1,160,000, 1 bedroom — AED 2,350,000, 2 bedrooms — AED 3,500,000. This is the median across all deals in the area, not a valuation of a specific unit.

Q: What share of deals in Dubai Islands are off-plan?
A: 97% of sales in Dubai Islands over the last 12 months were off-plan purchases, according to DLD data.

Q: How do Dubai Islands differ from Palm Jumeirah?
A: The Palm is established and pricier; Dubai Islands are a new area by the old city with a lower entry price and more projects under construction.

Q: Who builds here?
A: The master developer is Nakheel; private developers such as Imtiaz also build residential projects.

## Arjan: off-plan property and the area

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/areas/arjan/

Arjan is a residential district within Dubailand, next to Dubai Miracle Garden and Dubai Butterfly Garden. It has many new mid-rise buildings with studios and one- and two-bedroom apartments.

- Next to Dubai Miracle Garden and the Butterfly Garden.

- Mid-rise residential buildings.

- An affordable entry price, popular with investors.

- Samana, Danube, Iman and others are building actively.

### What the area is like
Arjan lies between Al Khail Road and Umm Suqeim Road, close to JVC and Al Barsha South. There is a hospital, schools and shopping centres nearby.

### Who it suits
Investors with budgets up to AED 1–1.5 million buying for long-term rental, and buyers looking for a new apartment at a moderate price.

### Transport
Easy access to Al Khail Road and Umm Suqeim Road; Dubai Marina and Mall of the Emirates are about a 15–20-minute drive. There is no metro in the area.

### What homes are sold here
Studios and one- to three-bedroom apartments in mid-rise buildings; many projects have pools, gyms and co-working spaces, and Samana offers private balcony pools.

Q: How much does a square metre cost in Arjan?
A: According to the Dubai Land Department (DLD), the median sale price in Arjan over the last 12 months is AED 16,968 per m² (data as of 2026-10-03). In 2023 the median was AED 12,456 per m².

Q: How much is an apartment in Arjan?
A: Median DLD transaction prices over 12 months in Arjan: studio — AED 730,000, 1 bedroom — AED 1,180,000, 2 bedrooms — AED 1,680,000. This is the median across all deals in the area, not a valuation of a specific unit.

Q: What share of deals in Arjan are off-plan?
A: 64% of sales in Arjan over the last 12 months were off-plan purchases, according to DLD data.

Q: How is Arjan similar to JVC?
A: Both are affordable and popular with investors; Arjan is younger and has more projects under construction.

Q: What yields are typical here?
A: Yields depend on the project and purchase price; compare them with neighbouring JVC and Al Barsha South in PromptEstates project cards.

## JVT: off-plan property and the area

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/areas/jvt/

Jumeirah Village Triangle (JVT) is a Nakheel residential community next to JVC. It has more villas and townhouses, and new projects include mid-rise apartment buildings.

- Next door to JVC; master developer Nakheel.

- Many villas and townhouses; quieter and greener.

- New mid-rise building projects.

- Object 1 and other private developers are building here.

### What the area is like
JVT is laid out as a triangle of villa clusters around parks. In recent years more and more mid-rise residential projects have appeared.

### Who it suits
Families who want a quieter life than in JVC, and investors looking for new apartments in an established area with moderate prices.

### Transport
The area is by Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Al Khail Road; Dubai Marina is about a 15-minute drive. There is no metro in the area.

### What homes are sold here
Ready villas and townhouses, plus new mid-rise buildings with studios and one- and two-bedroom apartments.

Q: How much does a square metre cost in Jumeirah Village Triangle (JVT)?
A: According to the Dubai Land Department (DLD), the median sale price in Jumeirah Village Triangle (JVT) over the last 12 months is AED 17,979 per m² (data as of 2026-10-03). In 2023 the median was AED 14,404 per m².

Q: How much is an apartment in Jumeirah Village Triangle (JVT)?
A: Median DLD transaction prices over 12 months in Jumeirah Village Triangle (JVT): studio — AED 780,000, 1 bedroom — AED 1,240,000, 2 bedrooms — AED 1,720,000. This is the median across all deals in the area, not a valuation of a specific unit.

Q: What share of deals in Jumeirah Village Triangle (JVT) are off-plan?
A: 85% of sales in Jumeirah Village Triangle (JVT) over the last 12 months were off-plan purchases, according to DLD data.

Q: JVT or JVC?
A: JVT is quieter with more villas; JVC is denser with apartments and has more projects. Off-plan prices are comparable.

Q: Is JVT good for renting out?
A: Yes, it is popular with families; compare demand and yield for the specific project.

## Al Furjan: off-plan property and the area

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/areas/al-furjan/

Al Furjan is a Nakheel residential community near Ibn Battuta Mall and Discovery Gardens. With the opening of the Route 2020 metro line the area got its own station.

- Between Sheikh Zayed Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road.

- Al Furjan metro station on the Route 2020 line.

- Villas, townhouses and new residential buildings.

- Imtiaz, Azizi, Danube and others are building here.

### What the area is like
Al Furjan started as a villa and townhouse community and now has many mid-rise residential buildings. Ibn Battuta Mall, Dubai Marina and JLT are about a 15-minute drive away.

### Who it suits
Families who value the metro and a calm setting, and investors looking for liquid apartments for long-term rental at a moderate price.

### Transport
Metro stations on the Route 2020 line and access to Sheikh Zayed Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road. Dubai Marina and JLT are about 15 minutes away.

### What homes are sold here
Apartments in new mid-rise buildings, as well as villas and townhouses. Many projects are handed over furnished with shared amenities.

Q: What share of deals in Al Furjan are off-plan?
A: 51% of sales in Al Furjan over the last 12 months were off-plan purchases, according to DLD data.

Q: What makes Al Furjan convenient to live in?
A: The metro, nearby shopping centres and a calm family setting at moderate prices.

Q: Who builds here?

## DAMAC Hills: off-plan property and the area

URL: https://promptestates.com/en/areas/damac-hills/

DAMAC Hills is a gated community by developer DAMAC around the Trump International Golf Club Dubai course. It has villas, townhouses and apartments overlooking the golf course and parks.

- A community by developer DAMAC.

- Trump International Golf Club Dubai at its centre.

- Villas, townhouses and apartments.

- Parks, schools and sports facilities within the community.

### What the area is like
DAMAC Hills sits off Al Qudra Road and Hessa Street, near Arjan and Motor City. Inside the community are the golf course, parks, schools and shops.

### Who it suits
Families who want a villa or townhouse in a green gated community, and those who value golf and sport close to home. Do not confuse it with the separate DAMAC Hills 2 community.

### Transport
Access to Al Qudra Road, Hessa Street and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road; Dubai Marina and Downtown are about a 20–25-minute drive. There is no metro.

### What homes are sold here
Villas and townhouses, plus apartments in complexes overlooking the golf course. DAMAC keeps launching new phases.

Q: How much does a square metre cost in DAMAC Hills?
A: According to the Dubai Land Department (DLD), the median sale price in DAMAC Hills over the last 12 months is AED 18,297 per m² (data as of 2026-10-03). In 2023 the median was AED 15,819 per m².

Q: How much is an apartment in DAMAC Hills?
A: Median DLD transaction prices over 12 months in DAMAC Hills: studio — AED 610,000, 1 bedroom — AED 1,240,000, 2 bedrooms — AED 2,010,000. This is the median across all deals in the area, not a valuation of a specific unit.

Q: What share of deals in DAMAC Hills are off-plan?
A: 51% of sales in DAMAC Hills over the last 12 months were off-plan purchases, according to DLD data.

Q: Are DAMAC Hills and DAMAC Hills 2 the same?
A: No. DAMAC Hills is the community around the golf club off Al Qudra Road; DAMAC Hills 2 is a separate, more remote and more affordable area.

Q: Is it good for families?
A: Yes: there are schools, parks, sports facilities and shops inside.

## Emaar Properties: projects and off-plan homes

- Founded in 1997; listed on the Dubai Financial Market.

- Develops Dubai Hills Estate, Dubai Creek Harbour and Emaar Beachfront.

- Builds apartments, townhouses and villas in master-planned communities.

- Founded in 2002.

- Linked to the Government of Dubai; part of Dubai Holding.

- Part of Dubai Holding.

- Azizi Venice — a large lagoon project in Dubai South.

## Object 1: projects and off-plan homes
